title: kb_backlog_write's docs name what its call does not check: user-level and managed settings, the coord hook's claim notice, and --by operator on operator-only classes other than ceiling
goal: kb/_self/backlog.md or plugin.md says, beside KB_BACKLOG_WRITE_TOOLS, that the deny check reads only the clone's two settings files, that a call made through kb_backlog_write skips the PreToolUse Bash hook's backlog-claim notice, and that --by operator is accepted on every operator-only class except ceiling, as on the command line in an agent session

run:
import re
t = open("kb/_self/backlog.md", encoding="utf-8").read() + open("kb/_self/plugin.md", encoding="utf-8").read()
paras = [p for p in t.split("\n") if "KB_BACKLOG_WRITE_TOOLS" in p]
assert paras, "no doc line names KB_BACKLOG_WRITE_TOOLS"
low = " ".join(paras).lower()
miss = [w for w in ("user-level", "coord", "--by operator") if w not in low]
assert not miss, ("the docs of kb_backlog_write do not name these limits", miss)

notes: Planner (SP-fn7letri): the goal names docs only, so _tools/kb_mcp.py left the touches; the item changes kb/_self/backlog.md or plugin.md text beside KB_BACKLOG_WRITE_TOOLS.
